title: Rails Active Storage NUL-byte filenames can cause persistent denial of service
summary: Active Storage stores client-supplied filenames verbatim. On SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB, a permitted uploader can persist a filename containing a NUL byte; calls to File.basename or File.extname then raise ArgumentError when variants, previews or attachments are rendered, potentially disabling affected pages until the filename is purged or corrected. PostgreSQL rejects the row and is not affected.
ai_role: The Rails advisory directly says the issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner, identifier ANT-2026-UQM5Z4YL. The source does not identify the model or detail validation steps.
classification_note: The maintainer published GHSA-p2pm-g2h6-7j5j on 2026-11-04 and lists CVE-2026-126074. The advisory describes an availability vulnerability and does not assert exploitation.
remediation_note: The advisory lists Active Storage 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 as patched and provides patches. The persistent failure can also be cleared by purging the affected blob or correcting its filename; PostgreSQL rejects the problematic row.
